suggestions.title: Put Tuesday's leg extension back — with the load on it

rationale.science: A double-progression gate can only rule on what it can see, and your app's own two-for-two rule exists because a single top-of-window sighting sits inside the 0.9-1.4 rep prediction error of one set (Mitter 2022; Ratamess 2009). A set the engine cannot read cannot earn anything.
rationale.data: Your feed for 8/4 reads 'RECORD AMENDED - Leg extension UN-SKIPPED on Tue 8/4 - logged 8,8'. But sessionLog['2026-08-04'] has five entries and extension is not among them - it sits in that day's skipped list; exercises.extension.lastMeta still reads 2026-07-31, 150 x 10,9; ex.last still reads [10,9]; and q_ext155 still sits at DEBUT, not done.
rationale.relationship: mergeState scores a session by entry count, so an un-skip that ADDS an entry wins and a re-skip that REMOVES one can win right back - which is exactly the failure mode you wrote into NEXT.md last night. The 8,8 survived in the feed, which nothing reads, and died in the log, which everything reads.

suggestions.predict: Re-enter it with the weight and one of two things settles tonight. At 155, 8,8 meets the clean-debut threshold this loop named on 8/1, q_ext155 closes and the gate CL-2 shut on 7/21 is earned. At 150, it is three reps off your 10,9 and the gate stays shut. Either way exercises.extension.lastMeta moves off 2026-07-31 and your next lower day stops prescribing from a nine-day-old card.

suggestions.title: Open rows at 2 RIR next upper day — it is frozen until you do

apply.to: Rows 180: log the opener at 2 RIR next upper day to release the governor hold

rationale.science: On a deficit you defend load rather than chase failure - work taken to failure costs recovery it does not repay (Robinson 2024; Grgic 2021), and RIR autoregulation is the one readiness method with outcome evidence behind it (Helms 2018; Larsen 2021).
rationale.data: exercises.rows.rirHist reads [0,0] - your opener went to 0 RIR on 7/30 and again on 8/3 - and holdFlag is true. Your own recovery card names it: '1 lift held by the governor: Rows (strapless).' While that flag stands, progressStep returns a step of zero and the load queue is blocked even at the top of the window.
rationale.relationship: Two hot openers in a row set the flag; a single opener logged at 1 RIR or better clears it the moment it lands, and the app writes 'HOLD RELEASED - loads can earn.' This is the one place your 0-RIR week actually cost you something, and it cost progression rather than reps.

suggestions.predict: Open rows at 2 RIR next upper day - roughly 180 x 8 rather than 9 - and the hold releases in that session, putting 185 back in reach off 10,10. Leave the opener hot and 180 cannot climb however good the reps look, which is a slower and much less obvious way to lose the lift.

suggestions.title: Ham's top-of-window counter is a fourth cache — it is one sighting ahead of the log

rationale.science: Your app requires two sightings at the top of the window before a load queues, on the ACSM progression precedent (Ratamess 2009), because one sighting cannot be told apart from a good day inside your own set-to-set spread (Mitter 2022). A counter carrying a sighting the log no longer supports defeats that safeguard rather than applying it.
rationale.data: exercises.ham reads topAt 120 / topRun 1, but the most recent ham session at 120 is Tuesday's 10,10 - well below the 12,11 the window needs - and your own code resets topRun to 0 on exactly that case. Last night's reconcileLiftCaches healed lastMeta and ex.last; it does not touch topAt or topRun.
rationale.relationship: The un-skip path rebuilds the two caches you fixed and never runs the progression step, so the counters it feeds are left behind. Next honest 12,11 therefore computes a run of two and queues 125 off one real session - the unearned-bump shape that cratered your extension at 155 in July.

suggestions.predict: Clear topRun (or let a filed non-top ham session clear it) and 125 waits for two real sightings, the way the rule intends. Leave it and the very next good ham day queues a 4% jump on a lift that just did 10,10 after a week off.
